name: Launch Environment Performance Requirement
text: The equipment shall be designed to function within performance specifications after exposure in the launch configuration to the maximum launch or other nonorbital service environments. These environments include temperature, vibration, acoustic noise, shock, acceleration, atmospheric pressure, humidity, and electrical storms with associated radiation.

name: Launch Temperature Design Requirement
text: The design shall be capable of withstanding thermal environments during launch preparations and launch which are between 10 deg C (18 deg F) above the maximum predicted temperature and 10 deg C (18 deg F) below the minimum predicted temperature.

name: Random Vibration Design Margin
text: A random vibration environment that is 6 decibels (dB) above the maximum predicted levels shall be used to provide the required design margin of safety.

name: Vibration Exposure Duration Requirement
text: This design environment shall be considered to persist for three times the exposure duration associated with environmental amplitudes that are greater than one half the maximum predicted environmental amplitudes, but for not less than three minutes, along each of the three orthogonal axes.

name: Acoustic Environment Substitution Requirement
text: An acoustic design environment that is 6 dB above the maximum predicted levels shall be used instead of the mechanical vibration environment for components where mechanical vibration would not simulate imposition of the service environment.

name: Sinusoidal Vibration Design Margin
text: In cases where higher frequency sinusoidal vibration is present, the design levels shall be 6 dB above the maximum predicted levels in order to provide the required design margin of safety.

name: Shock Spectrum Design Requirement
text: The design shock spectrum shall be at least 6 dB over the maximum predicted pyrotechnic shock levels.

name: Acceleration Design Level Requirement
text: The design acceleration level shall be the maximum predicted level multiplied by an ultimate factor of safety that includes a 10 percent test measurement tolerance.

name: Launch Acceleration Ultimate Factors of Safety
text: The launch design acceleration ultimate factor of safety shall be at least 1.38 (1.25 + 10 percent) for unmanned vehicles and 1.54 (1.40 + 10 percent) for manned vehicles.

name: Yield Factor of Safety Requirement
text: Unless otherwise specified, the yield factor of safety shall be 1.0.

name: Positive Strength Margins Requirement
text: All yield and ultimate strength margins of safety shall be positive.

name: Cross-Axis Acceleration Requirement
text: When applicable, the cross axis design acceleration shall include the acceleration due to rotation.

name: Atmospheric Pressure Change Requirement
text: The design shall be capable of sustaining ambient pressures that change from sea level to 0.0133 pascals (1.929 X 10-6 pounds per square inch) in 3 minutes.

name: Humidity and Mildly Corrosive Environment Exposure Requirement
text: The design shall, where practicable, be capable of sustaining exposures up to 12 hours in duration to moderately humid or mildly corrosive environments while unprotected during manufacture or handling, such as possible industrial environments or sea coast fog that could be expected prior to launch.

name: On-Orbit Environmental Design Margin
text: The equipment shall be designed to function within performance specifications following or, if appropriate, during exposure to environmental levels that exceed the maximum predicted on-orbit environments by the design factor of safety or design margin. These environments include thermal, vacuum, radiation exposure, shock, random vibration, and acceleration.

name: Thermal and Vacuum Operating Range
text: The moving mechanical assemblies shall operate at any temperature within their thermal design range, at an ambient pressure less than 133 micropascals (1.93 x 10-7 psi). The thermal design range is from 10 deg C (18 deg F) above the maximum predicted temperature to 10 deg C (18 deg F) below the minimum predicted temperature.

name: Minimum Thermal Design Range Requirement
text: In addition, the thermal design range shall not be less than from +71 deg C to -34 deg C (160 deg F to -29 deg F) unless attainment of this capability would not be practicable or would adversely influence the design, such as necessitating the use of a less desirable lubricant.

name: Radiation Exposure Performance Requirement
text: The moving mechanical assemblies shall be designed to operate within performance specifications after exposure to on-orbit level radiation environments for the service life of the assembly.

name: Radiation Timeline Design Margin
text: The timeline of the on-orbit levels shall include a representative number of time periods at the maximum predicted radiation levels to ensure a satisfactory design margin.

name: On-Orbit Shock Spectrum Requirement
text: The design level pyrotechnic shock spectrum shall be at least 6 dB over the maximum predicted levels occurring during on-orbit operation.

name: On-Orbit Random Vibration Design Level
text: The on-orbit random vibration design level shall be at least 6 dB above the maximum predicted on-orbit levels.

name: On-Orbit Acceleration Design Level
text: The on-orbit acceleration design level shall be the maximum predicted on-orbit levels multiplied by a factor of safety that includes a 10 percent test measurement tolerance.

name: Minimum On-Orbit Acceleration Factor of Safety
text: The on-orbit design acceleration factor of safety shall be at least two.

name: Acceleration Due to Vehicle Rotation
text: When applicable, the acceleration shall include that which is due to vehicle rotation.

name: Clean Room Environment for Fabrication and Handling
text: Fabrication and handling of moving mechanical assemblies shall be accomplished in a clean room environment with an air cleanliness that is in accordance with metric system class 3500 (English system class 100,000) or better as specified in FED-STD-209.

name: Processing and Storage Environmental Limits
text: Environmental conditions during processing and during storage, prior to acceptance testing, shall be within the following limits: Temperature: 21 deg C +/- 20 deg C; Humidity: 50 percent +/- 40 percent.

name: Post-Acceptance Storage, Handling, and Transportation Conditions
text: Storage, handling, and transportation conditions to which items are to be subjected subsequent to acceptance testing, and prior to flight, shall be controlled to environmental conditions which do not exceed the maximum predicted requirements imposed by launch, flight, or the specified acceptance tests.

name: Protection of Molybdenum Dry Film Lubricated Bearings
text: Critical bearing surfaces employing molybdenum dry film lubricants shall be protected by a dry nitrogen purge or other suitable means of excluding humidity during the storage and pre-launch environment.

name: Nameplate Identification Requirement
text: Each moving mechanical assembly and interchangeable subassembly shall be identified by a nameplate. The nameplate identification may be attached to, etched in, or marked directly on the item where size and noninterference of operation permits.

name: Nameplate Legibility Requirement
text: The nameplate shall utilize suitable letter size and contrasting colors, contrasting surface finishes, or other techniques to provide identification that is readily legible.

name: Nameplate Durability Requirement
text: The nameplate shall be capable of withstanding cleaning procedures and environmental exposures anticipated during the service life of the item without becoming illegible. Metal foil nameplates may be applied if they can be placed in an area where they cannot interfere with proper operation should they inadvertently become detached.

name: Prohibition on Metal Stamping
text: Metal stamping shall not be used.

name: Nameplate Visibility Requirement
text: Where practicable, identification nameplates on components and subassemblies shall be in locations which permit observation of the marking at the next higher level of assembly.

name: Nameplate Minimum Content Requirements
text: Nameplates shall contain, as a minimum, the following: a. Item identification number b. Serial number c. Lot number d. Manufacturer e. Nomenclature

name: Interchangeability Marking Requirement
text: The marking of any two or more items intended for space applications with the same item number or identification shall indicate that they may be capable of being changed, one for another, without alteration of the items themselves or of adjoining equipment if the items also meet the specified flight accreditation requirements.

name: Referenced Nameplate Information Accompaniment
text: A copy of the referenced nameplate information or card shall accompany the item or assembly containing the item during ground tests and ground operations.

name: Red Tag or Red Paint for Non-Flight Items
text: Items which by intent or by material disposition are not suitable for use in flight, and which could be accidentally substituted for flight or flight spare hardware, shall be red tagged or striped with red paint, or both, to prevent such substitution.

name: NOT FOR FLIGHT Tag Marking Requirement
text: The red tag shall be conspicuous and marked "NOT FOR FLIGHT."

name: Red Paint Compatibility and Visibility
text: The red paint shall be material compatible and the stripes unmistakable.

name: Clearance Requirements Establishment
text: The clearance requirements between the moving mechanical assembly or deployable and any other structure or component shall be established and maintained.

name: Clearance Adequacy Considerations
text: The manufacturing, assembly, and alignment tolerances as well as environmental conditions such as temperature, temperature gradients, vibration, distortion due to relaxation of the "g" field, effects of centrifugal forces, and acceleration during the critical periods of launch and on-orbit operations shall be taken into consideration for establishing clearance adequacy.

name: Clearance Maintenance During All Modes
text: The established clearances shall be maintained during transportation and all operational modes of the vehicle.

name: Avoidance of Sensor Field-of-View Obscuration
text: Obscuration of the operational fields of view of vehicle sensors by the moving mechanical assemblies shall be avoided except where obscuration is a design requirement of the sensor system.

name: Interface Control Drawings for Deployable Positions
text: Interface control drawings or layouts shall indicate the stowed, extended, and critical intermediate positions of the moving mechanical assemblies and deployables with respect to fields of view and surrounding structure or components.

name: Alignment and Adjustment Provisions
text: Provisions shall be included to permit alignment and adjustment of moving mechanical assemblies with respect to the vehicle and other subsystem elements where appropriate. A shimming-type alignment technique may be used where additional surface area is necessary to provide a bearing surface or where electrical bonding is required.

name: Locking Provisions for Adjustable Alignments
text: Where an adjustable type alignment technique is used, locking provisions as specified herein shall be provided.

name: Preference for Simple Structural Interfaces
text: In selecting the design for the structural interface of the moving mechanical assembly with the vehicle, preference shall be given to simple approaches that minimize the complexity of the interface.

name: Ease of Installation and Accessibility
text: The moving mechanical assembly shall, where practicable, be easily installed and readily accessible for inspection or removal.

name: Standard Wrench Clearances
text: Standard wrench clearances shall be provided.

name: Minimization of Special Tools
text: The use of special tools shall be minimized.

name: Minimum Fitting Factor for Complex Interfaces
text: In addition, where complex connections and structural assembly interfaces are employed, the design of fittings shall be based on a minimum fitting factor of 1.15 at ultimate load.

name: Common Interface Drill Template
text: Where practicable, a common interface drill template shall be used to ensure correct mechanical mating, particularly for interfaces external to the moving mechanical assembly.

name: Interchangeability of Mechanical Assemblies
text: Any two or more moving mechanical assemblies bearing the same part number or identification shall possess such functional and physical characteristics as to be equivalent in performance and durability and shall be capable of being changed, one for another, without alterations of the items themselves or of adjoining items except for alignment adjustments.

name: Reliability Allocations and Design Requirements
text: The reliability allocations to the moving mechanical assemblies and the assigned design requirements shall ensure that the overall vehicle reliability requirements are met under the severe extremes of acceptance testing, storage, transportation, preflight testing, and operational environments. Highly reliable assemblies are usually obtained by elimination of single point failure modes unless it can be shown that the addition of redundancy actually reduces overall reliability due to added complexity. The incorporation of redundancy is usually an acceptable technique for meeting the reliability requirements.

name: Reliability Determination for Autonomous Switching Designs
text: For designs that switch redundant subassemblies or units autonomously, or by ground command, the failure rates for the switching circuits, and for the redundant equipment while in the off line mode, shall be appropriately included in the reliability determination.

name: Analytical Reliability Determination
text: The reliability of each moving mechanical assembly shall be analytically determined using piece part or component failure rates obtained from actual usage data where available, or evaluated at anticipated operating temperatures from standard data sources such as MIL-HDBK-217.

name: Reliability Evaluation in Terms of Events and Usage Cycles
text: The assembly reliability shall be evaluated in terms of events and usage cycles that occur in operation.

name: Design Margins to Prevent Wear-Out
text: The design margins shall preclude wear out of components within the service life of the vehicle at the programmed duty cycle, including the wear associated with all preflight testing.

name: No Scheduled Maintenance Requirement
text: Except for possible relubrication after extended storage, or at prescribed intervals in multiple reuse applications, the moving mechanical assemblies shall, where practicable, be designed so as not to require any scheduled maintenance or repair during their service life.

name: Validation of No Scheduled Maintenance
text: Suitable development tests and inspections at appropriate intervals shall validate that scheduled maintenance is not required.

name: Access for Replacement of Age-Dated Elastomeric Materials
text: However, access shall be provided for replacement of age-dated elastomeric materials which may have "expiration of useful life" dates that can occur before scheduled flight.

name: Human Engineering Criteria Application
text: Throughout the design and development of the moving mechanical assemblies, criteria shall be judiciously applied to obtain effective, compatible, and safe man-equipment interactions.

name: Design for Testability and Inspection
text: The design of all moving mechanical assemblies shall be such that they may be tested or inspected to ensure that they are assembled and installed correctly.

name: Incorrect Assembly Prevention Features
text: Provisions such as tabs, shoulders, and different thread sizes shall be employed to prevent assembly in any incorrect manner which may impair the intended functions of the moving mechanical assembly.

name: Service Life Exceeds Vehicle Life
text: The combined operational and nonoperational service life of the moving mechanical assemblies shall exceed the service life of the vehicle in which they are mounted. The service life includes all operational and nonoperational time required or allowed after successful completion of acceptance tests.

name: General Safety Hazard Prevention
text: The design shall be such that a safety hazard to personnel and surrounding equipment shall not be created during installation, maintenance, ground test, and transportation of moving mechanical assemblies and deployables.

name: Protection from Damage During All Stages
text: Moving mechanical assemblies, particularly those associated with deployables, shall be protected from damage which may occur at any stage of the fabrication, assembly, testing, or transportation.

name: Precautions for Deployed Positions
text: When deployables are in their deployed positions, special precautions such as restrictions on the activities of personnel in the immediate area and exclusion of others by means of personnel barriers shall be used.

name: Precautions to Prevent Dropped Tools
text: During installation, maintenance, ground test, and transportation, precautions shall be taken to preclude the dropping of tools or other items that might injure personnel or damage sensitive equipment. Tethering of tools to the person or clothing is recommended.

name: Use of Protective Covers and Devices
text: In addition, protective covers or other protective devices shall be incorporated, where appropriate.

name: Safety Procedures for Explosive Ordnance
text: Required safety procedures for handling, storing, and testing explosive ordnance shall be documented and implemented where applicable.

name: STS Payload Safety Requirements
text: For all moving mechanical assemblies and deployables that are in payloads which are to be launched by the Space Transportation System (STS), the safety requirements shall also be in accordance with Chapter 2 of NHB 1700.7 (NASA). For these payloads, it is required that the payload must tolerate a minimum number of failures and operator errors determined by the consequence of any hazardous functions.

name: Catastrophic Hazard Control for STS Payloads
text: For catastrophic hazards or hazards that would result in personnel injury, loss of the orbiter, or loss of STS facilities and equipment, the hazard shall be controlled such that no combination of two failures, operator errors, or radio frequency signals would unleash the hazard.

name: Controlled Handling and Storage of Parts and Materials
text: Handling and storage of parts and materials for space applications shall be controlled consistent with the criticality of the end use of each item.

name: Controlled Environment and Access
text: Controlled environment and controlled access shall be used to the extent required to avoid degradation of the quality and reliability of the parts, materials, and assemblies.

name: Manufacturing Process Compliance
text: The manufacturing process shall be accomplished in accordance with documented procedures and process controls which ensure the reliability and quality required for the mission.

name: Documentation of Manufacturing Procedures
text: These manufacturing procedures and process controls shall be documented to give visibility to the procedures and specifications by which all processes, operations, inspections, and tests are to be accomplished by the contractor.

name: Documentation of Parts, Materials, and Entry Points
text: This internal contractor documentation shall include the name of each part or component, each material required, the point it enters the manufacturing flow, and the controlling specification or drawing.

name: Documentation of Tooling, Facilities, and Verification
text: The documentation shall indicate required tooling, facilities, and test equipment; the manufacturing check points and pertinent process control thresholds; the quality assurance verification points; and the verification procedures corresponding to each applicable process or material listed.

name: Documentation Reflects Current Revisions
text: The specifications, procedures, drawings, and supporting documentation shall reflect the specific revisions in effect at the time the items were produced.

name: Manufacturing Process Control Baseline Retention
text: These flow charts and the referenced specifications, procedures, drawings, and supporting documentation become the manufacturing process control baseline and shall be retained by the contractor for reference.

name: Recording Changes to Manufacturing Baseline
text: All changes to the baseline processes used, or the baseline documents used, shall be recorded by the contractor following establishment of the manufacturing baseline or following the manufacture of the first item or lot of items. These changes provide the basis for flight accreditation of the items manufactured or of subsequent flight items.

name: Traceability for Failure and Discrepancy Analysis
text: The manufacturing process and control documents shall provide a contractor-controlled baseline that ensures that any subsequent failure or discrepancy analysis that may be required can identify the specific manufacturing materials and processes that were used for each item.

name: Grouping Parts into Production Lots
text: To the extent practicable, parts for use in space equipment shall be grouped together in individual production lots during the various stages of their manufacture to ensure that all devices assembled during the same time period use the same materials, tools, methods, and controls.

name: Lot Controls for Non-Testable Items
text: Parts and devices for space equipment that cannot be adequately tested after assembly without destruction of the item, such as explosive ordnance devices, shall have lot controls implemented during their manufacture to ensure a uniform quality and reliability level of the entire lot.

name: Single-Batch Manufacturing Requirement
text: Each lot shall be manufactured, tested, and stored as a single batch.

name: Sequential Lot Number Assignment
text: Sequential lot numbers that indicate the date of manufacture shall be assigned to each production lot.

name: Clean Environment for Fabrication and Handling
text: Fabrication and handling of space equipment shall be accomplished in a clean environment.

name: Avoidance of Chemical and Particulate Contamination
text: Attention shall be given to avoiding nonparticulate (chemical) as well as particulate air contamination.

name: Minimization of Liquid Use Near Explosive Devices
text: To avoid safety and contamination problems, the use of liquids shall be minimized in areas where initiators, explosive bolts, or any loaded explosive devices are exposed.

name: Internal Particulate Cleanliness Level
text: The particulate cleanliness of internal moving subassemblies shall be maintained to at least level 500 as defined in MIL-STD-1246.

name: External Surface Cleanliness
text: External surfaces shall be visibly clean.

name: Nonvolatile Residue Cleanliness Level
text: The allowable product nonvolatile residue (NVR) level shall be maintained to at least level "G", as defined in MIL-STD-1246.

name: Assembly-Specific Cleanliness Requirements
text: Specific cleanliness requirements shall be determined for each moving mechanical assembly based on an analysis of overall system cleanliness requirements.

name: Bake-Out to Reduce Outgassing
text: Items that might otherwise produce deleterious outgassing while on orbit shall, where practicable, be baked for a sufficient time to drive out all but an acceptable level of outgassing products prior to installation in the assembly.

name: Vacuum Exposure for Outgassing Reduction
text: Where baking is not practicable, exposure to vacuum within the operating temperature of the item shall be employed.

name: Electrostatic Discharge Protection Requirements
text: Appropriate provisions stated in DOD-HDBK-263 shall be used to avoid and to protect against the effects of static electricity generation and discharge in areas containing electrostatic sensitive devices such as microcircuits, initiators, explosive bolts, or any loaded explosive device.

name: Grounding of Equipment and Personnel
text: Both equipment and personnel shall be grounded.

name: Craftsmanship Quality Requirements
text: Moving mechanical assemblies shall be manufactured, processed, tested, handled, and installed such that the finished items are of sufficient quality to ensure reliable operation, safety, and service life.

name: Freedom from Defects Affecting Operational Use
text: The items shall be free of defects that would interfere with operational use such as excessive scratches, nicks, burrs, loose material, contamination, and corrosion.

name: Controlled Storage, Handling, and Transportation Conditions
text: Storage, handling, and transportation conditions to which moving mechanical assemblies are to be subjected prior to flight shall be controlled to the limits of Paragraph 3.4.3.

name: Operational Readiness After Long-Term Storage
text: The items shall be capable of meeting the operational requirements without refurbishment, other than relubrication, after nonoperational storage of four years in a controlled environment (see 3.4.3).

name: Minimization of Oil Flow During Storage
text: The orientation or storage environment or both shall be chosen to minimize oil flow within the assembly.

name: Preferred No-Load Storage Condition
text: Storage shall preferably be in a "no-load" condition with springs in a relaxed state and pressure vessels unpressurized.

name: Documented Storage, Relubrication, and Retesting Procedures
text: The storage, relubrication, and retesting of all moving mechanical assemblies shall be in accordance with documented procedures.

name: Cleanliness During Storage and Transportation
text: Cleanliness shall be maintained during processing, storage, and transportation using appropriate protective containers or covers.

name: Antistatic Packaging for Electrostatic Sensitive Items
text: Electrostatic sensitive items, such as most electronic assemblies and components containing explosives, shall be stored and transported in sealed packages using antistatic wrapping material. The antistatic wrapping material used should not produce nonvolatile residues.

name: Grounding Antistatic Material Prior to Removal
text: The antistatic wrapping material shall be grounded through a resistor prior to removal.

name: Grounding Resistor Value Requirements
text: The grounding resistor shall have a value between 100,000 ohms and 1 megohm.

name: Monitoring Environmental Conditions and Shock Exposure
text: Temperature and humidity conditions and transportation shock exposure shall be monitored subsequent to manufacture, and the measured levels evaluated against the acceptance test limits.

name: Test and Inspection Facility Capability
text: The manufacturer shall ensure that test and inspection facilities of sufficient accuracy, quality, and quantity are established and maintained to permit performance of required inspections.

name: Control of Parts and Materials Prior to Assembly
text: To ensure that a reliable moving mechanical assembly is fabricated, all parts and materials shall be adequately controlled and inspected prior to assembly.

name: Control of Tools, Processes, Parts, and Materials During Fabrication
text: During fabrication, the tools and processes, as well as parts and materials, shall be adequately controlled and inspected to ensure compliance with the approved manufacturing processes and controls.

name: Accreditation Records Maintenance
text: Records documenting the accreditation status of the moving mechanical assemblies shall be maintained following assignment of serial numbers.

name: Serial Number Traceability Records
text: Each moving mechanical assembly shall have inspection records and test records maintained by serial number to provide trace-ability from system usage to production lot data for the device.

name: Complete Records Availability
text: Complete records shall be maintained and shall be available for review during the service life of the system.

name: Record Content Requirements
text: The records shall indicate all relevant test data, all rework or modifications, and all installation and removals for whatever reason.

name: In-Process Manufacturing Screens
text: Each moving mechanical assembly and each critical subassembly shall be subjected to in-process manufacturing and assembly screens to ensure compliance with the specified requirements to the extent practicable.

name: Verification of Process Controls and Configuration
text: Compliance with the documented process controls, documented screening requirements, required hardware configuration, and general workmanship requirements shall be verified.

name: Visual Inspection at Each Assembly Level
text: At each level of assembly, each completed unit shall be subjected to visual inspection to ensure that it is free of obvious defects and is within specified physical limits.

name: Reject Nonconforming Material
text: Nonconforming material, components, or assemblies that do not meet the established tolerance limits set for the acceptance limits in the in-process screens shall be rejected for use.

name: No Reassignment of Lot-Controlled Units
text: Reassignment of units that were lot controlled to a different lot shall not be made.

name: Scrap Nonconforming Material Not Meeting Rework Criteria
text: Nonconforming material or assembled units that do not satisfy these rework criteria shall be considered scrap.

name: Inspection of Castings, Welds, Composite Parts, and Stressed Surfaces
text: As a minimum, all castings, fusion welds, fibre composite or honeycomb parts and surfaces of stressed parts shall be inspected as follows:

name: Radiographic Inspection of Castings and Welds
text: All castings and all fusion welds shall be inspected for the presence of internal defects by radiographic methods in accordance with MIL-STD-453.

name: Internal Inspection of Composite Structures
text: Plastic composite structural elements shall be inspected for the presence of internal defects by an appropriate test method.

name: Surface Inspection of Stressed Parts
text: The surfaces of stressed parts shall be inspected in accordance with MIL-X-6868, MIL-STD-6866, or other appropriate inspection methods.

name: Nital Etch Inspection for High-Strength Steel
text: Heat-treated steel parts with tensile strength above 1,790 MPa that require a grinding operation after final heat treatment shall be inspected by Nital etch on all surfaces subject to grinding.

name: Complete Inspection of Critical or Single-Point-Failure Parts
text: All parts used in critical moving mechanical assemblies or parts comprising single point failures shall be completely inspected to ensure that no defects exist which could lead to degraded performance or failure.

name: Assembly Dimensional and Physical Inspection
text: The dimensions, weight, finish, identification markings, and cleanliness of each moving mechanical assembly shall be inspected, as appropriate, prior to acceptance testing and prior to installation on the vehicle.

name: Thread Engagement Requirements
text: Inspection of the assembly shall be made to ensure that a minimum thread engagement of five full threads exists for all threaded attachments; or where through bolts are used, that a minimum of two full threads protrude beyond the end of the nut.

name: Fastener Torque Inspection
text: Fasteners shall be inspected for compliance with required torque levels.

name: Concurrent Assembly Inspections
text: These inspections shall be made concurrently with the assembly of the parts.

name: Pin Puller Travel Verification
text: Pin pullers shall be inspected at the vehicle test level to verify adequate travel and travel margin.

name: Pre- and Post-Environmental Test Inspections
text: All moving mechanical assemblies shall be inspected before and after exposure to environmental tests at the component test level, at the vehicle test level, and at the launch site.

name: Inspection Processes
text: These inspection processes shall include, but are not limited to, the following: a. Scratched or damaged surfaces. b. Rust or corrosion. c. Fastener torque. d. Handling damage. e. Cleanliness. f. Wiring harness. g. Electrical and fluid connectors. h. Multilayer lnsulation. i. Safety wire. j. Alignment. k. Switches. l. Brinelling. m. Springs. n. Dampers. o. Clearances. p. Electric.

name: Surface Damage Rejection Criteria
text: If surface damage is sufficient to affect the intended function of the assembly, or the performance is degraded, the moving mechanical assembly shall be rejected.

name: Reject Rust or Corrosion
text: Any parts exhibiting rust or corrosion shall be rejected.

name: Fastener Looseness Inspection
text: Fasteners shall be visually inspected for looseness.

name: Torque Check Before and After Environmental Tests
text: The torque shall be checked on pre-selected fasteners before and after exposure to each environmental test condition.

name: Composite Part Damage Inspection
text: Graphite epoxy and other composite parts shall be visually inspected for damage.

name: Tubular Composite Internal Inspection
text: Where tubular composite members are used, the internal surfaces shall, where practicable, be visually inspected for damage, by means of a borescope or by other appropriate means.

name: Particulate Cleanliness Level
text: Product particulate cleanliness shall not exceed level 500 as defined in MIL-STD-1246.

name: Nonvolatile Residue Compliance
text: Product nonvolatile residue (NVR) shall be in compliance with the applicable requirements specified for each assembly.

name: Wiring Harness Security and Configuration
text: Wiring harnesses shall be inspected to verify that they are properly secured and to verify that the proper configuration is maintained, particularly in the area of rotating parts or joints.

name: Dust Caps on Unused Connectors
text: Dust caps shall be installed on unused connectors during shipment or test.

name: Connector Damage Inspection
text: Although unnecessary disconnecting and reconnecting of connectors shall be avoided, inspection for connector out-of-round and broken or loose electrical pins shall be made, where practicable.

name: MLI Clearance for Switch Operation
text: Where switches are used for indicating purposes, the clearance between the multilayer insulation and the switch shall be verified to ensure that proper operation of the switch can occur.

name: Safety Wire Installation Inspection
text: Fasteners utilizing safety wire shall be inspected to ensure that the wire is properly installed and that such wire cannot result in interference with other parts of the moving mechanical assembly.

name: Alignment Inspection
text: Alignment shall be inspected as appropriate.

name: Alignment Mirror Damage Inspection
text: Alignment mirrors shall be inspected to verify freedom from damage or displacement.

name: Deployable Alignment Verification
text: Alignments of deployables shall, where practicable, be checked in their deployed positions.

name: Indicating Switch Operation Inspection
text: Indicating switches shall be inspected to ensure that they operate satisfactorily and that adequate over-travel exists.

name: Switch Wire Damage Inspection
text: Switch wires shall be inspected to verify that they are free from damage or sharp bends.

name: Switch Actuation Continuity Verification
text: Switch actuation shall, where practicable, be verified by means of electrical continuity.

name: Brinelling Damage Inspection
text: Highly loaded surfaces such as preload fittings or over-center latches shall be inspected for evidence of Brinelling damage to surfaces in contact.

name: Spring Inspection and Measurement
text: Where accessibility permits, the following inspections and measurements shall be made on springs: inspection for broken coils or other damage and measurement of spring force or torque and spring rate on the fully assembled moving mechanical assembly.

name: Spring Load and Rate Pre-Assembly Measurement
text: The spring load at the installed position and the spring rate shall be measured before assembly, recorded, and the springs properly serialized.

name: Spring Load and Rate Post-Assembly Measurement
text: The spring load and the spring rate shall also be measured and recorded after spring assembly or installation, as appropriate.

name: Serialized Spring Location Recording
text: The location of each serialized spring on the moving mechanical assembly shall be recorded.

name: Spring Heat Treat Verification
text: On all springs comprising single point failures, the heat treat shall be checked, where practicable, using an unstressed portion of each spring, such as on the ground flats on the ends of compression springs.

name: Spring Position and Deflection Verification
text: Where practicable, actual spring position and deflected shape during the entire range of travel shall be checked to avoid off-nominal loading due to coil displacement and tang movement.

name: Viscous Damper Performance and Leak Check
text: Viscous dampers shall be performance and leak checked.

name: Deformable Damper Material Inspection
text: Deformable material dampers shall be inspected to ensure that the material is not deformed or damaged.

name: Clearance Inspection
text: Clearances shall be inspected to ensure compliance with the specified requirements.

name: Electric Motor Inspection and Measurement
text: Where accessibility permits, the following inspections and measurements shall be made on electric motors: 1. Verification of the part number. 2. Identification of special precautions (if any) such as use of keepers during armature removal, and observation of lead color code for polarity where suppression diodes are used. 3. Inspection for adequate lead length and clearance from other leads to which motor noise might introduce electromagnetic interference. 4. Adequate mount heat sinking. 5. Inspection of freedom of motion without binding or misalignment problems.

name: Establish Lubricant Processing Procedures
text: Lubricant processing procedures shall be established to control the uniformity, repeatability, cleanliness, accountability, and amount of lubricant in the moving mechanical assemblies.

name: Removal of Shipping Lubricants
text: Lubricant processing procedures shall delineate the processes of removal of bearing shipping lubricants.

name: Analyze Shipping Lubricant Compatibility
text: Shipping lubricants shall be analyzed for compatibility with the applied lubricant.

name: Replace Porous Retainers Containing Shipping Lubricants
text: Porous ball bearing retainers and lubricant reservoirs which have shipping lubricants in them shall be replaced before processing with the flight lubricant.

name: Wetability Testing of Bearings
text: Each bearing to be processed with a liquid lubricant shall be tested for wetability prior to application of the flight lubricant.

name: Approval of Wetability Test Method
text: The wetability test method shall be approved by the contracting officer.

name: Use Developmental Testing to Validate New Designs
text: Developmental testing shall be used to validate new design concepts for critical components and assemblies as a prelude to qualification testing.

name: Development Testing Must Ensure Minimal Failures During Qualification
text: The nature and extent of developmental testing on components, subsystems, and complete moving mechanical assemblies shall be sufficient to ensure that qualification testing of new designs will produce minimal failures which would then require redesign.

name: Development Testing Shall Use MIL-STD-1540 as a Guide
text: Developmental testing shall be conducted using MIL-STD-1540 as a guide.

name: Bearing Installation Design Substantiation
text: Unless the design is substantiated by previous usage, developmental testing shall include the following, as applicable: a. Tests to substantiate the design of each bearing installation with respect to materials, stresses, stiffness, fatigue life, preload, and possible binding under normal, as well as the most severe combined loading conditions, and the expected environmental conditions shall be conducted. b. For bearings that are reused, tests to characterize the wear and lubrication changes resulting from bearing reuse, and the effects these changes have on torque margin, shall be conducted.

name: Bearing Installation Tests
text: Tests to substantiate the design of each bearing installation with respect to materials, stresses, stiffness, fatigue life, preload, and possible binding under normal, as well as the most severe combined loading conditions, and the expected environmental conditions.

name: Bearing Reuse Substantiation
text: For bearings that are reused, tests to characterize the wear and lubrication changes resulting from bearing reuse, and the effects these changes have on torque margin, shall be conducted.

name: Temperature Gradient Effects on Bearing Preload
text: Where practicable, tests to substantiate the effects of temperature gradients on bearing preload and stiffness shall be conducted.

name: Lubricant System Adequacy Testing
text: For critical moving mechanical assemblies, tests of the lubricant that demonstrate the ability of the lubricant system to provide adequate lubrication under all specified operating conditions over the design lifetime shall be conducted.

name: Friction Welding Verification Tests
text: Where contact pressure is sufficiently high, such that friction welding might be possible, design and process verification tests shall be conducted at the piece part or subassembly level to verify the selection of materials and lubricants in the proposed application.

name: Brush and Commutator Lubrication and Wear Testing
text: For brushes and commutator or slip ring assemblies, tests shall demonstrate that the lubricant is not significantly deteriorated or driven from the areas requiring lubrication by adverse thermal, gravity forces, or other conditions; and that wear rates, wear debris, electrical noise level, friction torque, and lubricant loss are compatible with design requirements.

name: Deployable Driving Capability and Load Testing
text: For deployable devices, minimum available driving capability and maximum load determination shall be verified through an appropriate test program; each element of resistance shall be characterized in this test program.

name: Motor Torque vs Current Characterization
text: For moving mechanical assemblies driven by electrical motors, a torque versus current relationship for each motor under minimum, maximum, and ambient thermal and vacuum conditions shall be established.

name: Maintenance Substantiation
text: Where practicable, tests to substantiate that scheduled maintenance is not required.

name: Eddy Current Damper Life Testing
text: Eddy current dampers shall be tested for repeatability of damping rate and torque values for twice its expected operational life cycle.

name: Eddy Current Damper Temperature Testing
text: The eddy current damper shall be tested at temperature extremes to determine its damping rate over the temperature range.

name: First Assembly Inspection Requirement
text: An inspection of the first of each of the moving mechanical assemblies produced with production equipment and procedures shall be conducted at a time and location acceptable to the contracting officer.

name: No Discrepancies Among Equipment, Tooling, Drawings, and Records
text: There shall be no discrepancies among the equipment, the fabrication tooling used, the released drawings, the test data, the inspection records, and the specification requirements.

name: Verify Configuration and Workmanship Before Acceptance Testing
text: The configuration and workmanship of the completed hardware shall be verified by inspection prior to the start of acceptance testing.

name: Conduct Acceptance Tests per MIL-STD-1540
text: Acceptance tests shall be conducted on each moving mechanical assembly in accordance with the acceptance test requirements of MIL-STD-1540.

name: Acceptance Tests Shall Include Run-In, Functional, and Environmental Tests
text: The acceptance tests shall incorporate the run-in, functional, and environmental test requirements stated herein.

name: Acceptance Tests Must Detect Workmanship Defects
text: The acceptance tests shall be structured to detect workmanship defects that could affect operational performance.

name: Proof Testing of Composite or Honeycomb Components
text: Components fabricated from fiber composite material or of honeycomb construction shall be subjected to acceptance proof testing.

name: Acceptance Testing with Deployable Device Attached
text: The acceptance testing of moving mechanical assemblies that are part of a deployable device shall, where practicable, be conducted with the moving mechanical assembly attached to the deployable device.

name: Dummy Load Requirements for Acceptance Testing
text: The dummy loads shall provide a reasonable representation of the dynamic characteristics (such as inertia, stiffness, free play, and natural frequencies) of the actual driven member.

name: Account for Dummy Load Friction Effects
text: The effect of friction due to the additional weight of the dummy load on the drive unit shall be accounted for in evaluating the test results.

name: Torque and Angle Measurement Requirements
text: Appropriate quantitative measurements such as torque vs angle measurements and time vs angle measurements, or equivalent linear measurements for linear devices, shall be made during run-in, functional, and environmental acceptance testing of all moving mechanical assemblies.

name: Torque vs Angle Hysteresis for Spring-Driven Devices
text: For spring driven devices, torque vs angle measurements shall be made during restowing as well as during deployment in order to generate a torque vs angle hysteresis curve to determine torque margin.

name: Force Margin Measurements for Linear Devices
text: For linear devices, equivalent linear measurements shall be made to determine force margin.

name: Measurements Required at Ambient and Hot/Cold Acceptance Temperatures
text: As a minimum, these measurements shall be made under ambient and acceptance level hot and cold temperatures.

name: Redundant Modes Must Be Tested
text: Moving mechanical assemblies that contain redundancy in their design shall, where practicable, demonstrate performance to their requirements in each redundant mode of operation.

name: Functional Operation and Alignment Before and After Environmental Tests
text: Functional operation and alignment of each moving mechanical assembly, including instrumentation that is an integral part of the assembly, shall be tested and checked, where practicable, before and after exposure to each environmental acceptance test.

name: Swaged Ends Must Be Proof Tested
text: All swaged ends on rods or cables shall be 100 percent tested with a load equal to twice the limit load.

name: Run-In Test Required for Each Moving Mechanical Assembly
text: After initial functional testing, a run-in test shall be performed on each moving mechanical assembly before it is subjected to further acceptance testing, unless it can be shown that this procedure would be detrimental to performance and would result in reduced reliability.

name: Minimum Run-In Duration (Hours or Cycles)
text: The run-in test shall be conducted for a minimum of 50 hours except for items where the number of cycles of operation, rather than hours of operation, is a more appropriate measure of the capability to perform in a consistent and controlled manner.

name: Minimum Run-In Cycles Requirement
text: For these units, the run-in test shall be for at least 15 cycles or 5 percent of the total expected service life cycles, whichever is greater.

name: Periodic Measurements During Run-In
text: During the run-in test, sufficient periodic measurements shall be made to indicate what conditions may be changing with time and what wear rate characteristics exist.

name: Run-In Test Plan Approval
text: Test procedures, test time, and criteria for performance adequacy shall be in accordance with a test plan that has been approved by the contracting officer.

name: Post Run-In Inspection of Solid Film Lubricated Gear Trains
text: All gear trains using solid film lubricants shall, where practicable, be inspected and cleaned following the run-in test.

name: Functional and Environmental Tests Required
text: Each moving mechanical assembly shall be subjected to functional and environmental tests that are in accordance with the applicable acceptance test requirements of MIL-STD-1540.

name: Functional Tests Must Demonstrate Performance Requirements
text: Functional tests shall be structured to demonstrate that the moving mechanical assembly is capable of operating in such a manner that all performance requirements are satisfied.

name: Functional Tests Required Before and After Environmental Exposure
text: Functional tests are required before and after exposure to environmental test conditions in order to establish whether damage or degradation in performance has occurred.

name: Functional Tests Must Be Comprehensive
text: These tests shall be sufficiently comprehensive and shall include sufficient measurements to determine whether performance specifications are met.

name: Functional Tests Must Be Conducted in Relevant Environments
text: Where a device is designed to operate in extreme heat or cold or in some other environmental extreme, and a functional test at ambient conditions would not be significant, the functional tests shall be conducted in the appropriate environment that would demonstrate performance.

name: Test Assemblies in Launch or On-Orbit Configuration
text: The moving mechanical assemblies shall be tested in their launch or in their on-orbit configurations corresponding to the environment being simulated.

name: Assemblies Must Be Passive or Operating as in Launch/Orbit
text: They shall be passive or operating corresponding to their state during the launch or on-orbit operational phases.

name: Torque and Angle Measurements During Thermal Vacuum Testing
text: Fully assembled deployables shall, where practicable, have torque vs angle and time vs angle measurements, or equivalent linear measurements for linear devices, made during thermal vacuum testing.

name: Harmonic Drive Dedoidal Inspection
text: After a harmonic drive is assembled into the parent assembly, it shall be inspected for the dedoidal condition.

name: Hot/Cold Box Testing When Vacuum Testing Is Impractical
text: When operation of a deployable in a vacuum chamber or measurements in a vacuum chamber are impractical, the fully assembled deployable shall have deployment tests, including torque vs angle and time vs angle measurements, or equivalent linear measurements for linear devices, made in a hot or cold box.

name: Test Plan Approval for Functional and Environmental Tests
text: Test procedures, test time, and criteria for performance adequacy shall be as approved by the contracting officer.

name: No Disassembly or Repair Allowed During Testing Without Approval
text: No disassembly, adjustments, or repair shall be made on moving mechanical assemblies during functional and environmental acceptance testing or after completion of testing unless approved by the contracting officer.

name: Conduct Qualification Tests per MIL-STD-1540
text: The qualification tests of the moving mechanical assemblies shall be conducted in accordance with the qualification test requirements of MIL-STD-1540.

name: Qualification Tests Must Include Design Life, Functional, and Environmental Tests
text: The qualification tests shall incorporate the design life verification test, functional test, and environmental test requirements stated herein.

name: Dedicated Qualification Items Required for Multi-Use Assemblies
text: Moving mechanical assemblies which are required to operate more than once during their on-orbit life shall be tested using dedicated qualification items.

name: Flight Use of Qualification Article Requires Approval
text: Flight use of a qualification article shall have prior approval by the contracting officer.

name: Qualification Tests Must Demonstrate Design Adequacy and Margins
text: The qualification tests shall be structured to demonstrate the design adequacy and design margins.

name: Acceptance Test Must Precede Qualification Test
text: An acceptance test shall precede the qualification tests.

name: Torque and Angle Measurements Required During Qualification
text: Torque vs angle measurements and time vs angle measurements, or equivalent linear measurements for linear devices, shall be made during qualification testing of all moving mechanical assemblies.

name: Contracting Officer Approval Required for Alternate Qualification Evidence
text: Compliance with all or portions of the qualification requirements based upon tests of similar items or upon equivalent vehicle operational performance shall require approval of the contracting officer.

name: Qualification Test Configurations Must Match Acceptance Tests
text: The general test measurements and test configurations used for qualification tests shall be similar to those used for acceptance tests.

name: Redundant Modes Must Be Tested During Qualification
text: Moving mechanical assemblies that contain redundancy in their design shall, where practicable, demonstrate performance to their requirements in each redundant mode of operation during the qualification test.

name: Functional Operation and Alignment Before and After Qualification Tests
text: Functional operation and alignment of each moving mechanical assembly, including instrumentation that is an integral part of the assembly, shall, where practicable, be tested and checked, before and after exposure to each qualification test.

name: Design Life Verification Test Required
text: One or more items of each of the moving mechanical assemblies, produced with production equipment and procedures, shall be subjected to a design life verification test.

name: Simulate Worst Predicted Operational Environments
text: These tests shall be conducted to simulate operational use within the range of the worst predicted operational environments.

name: Demonstrate Full Operational Life Cycle Capability
text: The items shall be subjected to tests which demonstrate the capability to perform the full operational life cycle.

name: Simulate Operational Masses, Loads, and Stiffness
text: Masses, loads, and stiffness of support structure shall be actual or simulated operational values, and any interfacing equipment such as thermal heaters, cabling, or hoses shall be in place so that operational conditions are simulated.

name: Design Life Test Plan Approval
text: The test and criteria for performance adequacy shall be approved by the contracting officer.

name: Acceptable to Compress Duty Cycle for Low Duty Assemblies
text: For items having a relatively low percentage duty cycle, it shall be acceptable to compress the operational cycle into a tolerable total test duration.

name: Environmental Testing with Disassembly and Inspection
text: For such assemblies, tests shall be under proper environmental conditions, of varying duration, followed by disassembly and inspection.

name: Test Items Must Be Essentially Identical to Flight Items
text: The moving mechanical assemblies used for life test shall be essentially identical with the flight items.

name: Instrumentation Differences Must Not Jeopardize Validity
text: The only differences between the test items and the flight items shall be those changes necessary for incorporation of test instrumentation.

name: Validity
text: These differences shall not jeopardize the validity of the tests with respect to the flight hardware.

name: Instrumentation Required to Monitor Operating Conditions
text: Sufficient instrumentation shall be used to provide knowledge of the operating conditions within the assemblies during life testing such as internal pressures, temperatures, and temperature gradients.

name: Lubricant Monitoring During Life Test
text: Where liquid lubrication is used, consideration shall be given to measuring lubricant loss, degradation, distribution, quantity, and outgassing constituents over the duration of the test.

name: Instrumentation Consistency Across Test Phases
text: The instrumentation shall be similar to that employed in other test phases to provide a basis for comparison of the design life test conditions with those of other selected ground tests and with those during orbital operations.

name: Operate Assembly According to Predicted Duty Cycle
text: The design life test moving mechanical assembly shall be operated as expected in flight with equipment operating in accordance with the predicted duty cycle.

name: Include Variations of Expected Flight Usage
text: The tests shall include variations of the expected flight usage, such as power down modes to check low temperature operation of the system, to the degree practicable without exceeding the thermal limits of the equipment.

name: Slip Ring and Commutator Testing with Representative Current
text: All electrical slip ring and commutator assembly tests shall be conducted with representative levels of electrical current at the rated voltage across the interface.

name: Life Testing Duty Cycle Requirements
text: All moving mechanical assemblies shall be tested for at least twice the number of duty cycles expected in operational use, plus twice the number of duty cycles expected during component and vehicle functional and environmental tests.

name: Stop Testing Requirements
text: Stops shall be tested by intentionally running the moving mechanical assembly into the stops whether or not the moving mechanical assembly has limit switches to prevent contacting the stops in normal operation.

name: Stop Duty Cycle Requirements
text: The stops shall be tested for at least twice the number of duty cycles expected in operational use, plus twice the number of duty cycles expected during component and vehicle functional and environmental tests.

name: Functional Test After Life Verification
text: A functional test shall be conducted after the design life verification test has been completed and the assembly shall be disassembled and inspected for anomalous conditions.

name: Inspect Critical Areas for Fatigue Failure
text: The critical areas of parts which may be subject to fatigue failure shall be inspected to determine if failure has occurred.

name: Environmental Qualification Testing Required
text: One item of each of the moving mechanical assemblies, produced with production equipment and procedures, shall be subjected to environmental qualification testing to verify satisfactory performance at the design environmental levels.

name: Qualification Tests Shall Follow MIL-STD-1540
text: Tests shall be in accordance with the applicable qualification test requirements of MIL-STD-1540 (SSC-S-016).

name: Test Assemblies in Launch or On-Orbit Configuration
text: Moving mechanical assemblies shall be tested in their launch or in their on-orbit configurations corresponding to the environment being simulated.

name: Assemblies Shall Operate in Launch/Orbit State
text: Moving mechanical assemblies shall be passive or operating corresponding to their state during the launch or on-orbit operational phases.

name: Qualification Test Plan Approval
text: Test procedures, test time, and criteria for performance adequacy shall be as approved by the contracting officer.

name: Worst-Case Torque Margin Testing for Deployables
text: Qualification testing of deployables shall include tests to simulate the lowest motive force combined with the highest resistance under the most adverse environmental conditions to provide the worst case torque margin.

name: Worst-Case Loading Against Stops
text: The highest motive force combined with the lowest resistance under the most aiding environmental conditions shall be tested to provide the worst case loading including the loads against the stops.

name: Measurements Must Demonstrate Specification Compliance
text: Sufficient measurements shall be made to show that the requirements of this specification are met under both of the above conditions.

name: Torque and Angle Measurements Required
text: Measurements shall include torque vs angle and time vs angle, or equivalent linear measurements for linear devices.

name: Deployable Qualification Instrumentation Requirements
text: For deployables, time correlated video recording, or motion picture film coverage, and potentiometers, accelerometers, or other appropriate instrumentation shall be utilized for all functional and environmental qualification tests.

name: Pyrotechnic Release Test at 80% Charge
text: A one-time release test of pyrotechnic devices shall be conducted in the fully assembled configuration using a worst case lowest explosive charge loading of 80%.

name: Pyrotechnic Release Test Under Worst-Case Conditions
text: This release test shall be conducted using worst case tolerances and worst case environmental conditions.

name: Pyrotechnic Structural Damage Evaluation
text: To evaluate the possibility of structural damage to moving mechanical assemblies actuated by pyrotechnic devices, a one-time test shall also be conducted under worst case highest explosive charge loading.

name: Use 120% Charge for Structural Damage Test
text: A 120 percent explosive charge load shall, where practicable, be used for this test.

name: Shock Load Instrumentation Required
text: Instrumentation shall be provided on adjacent equipment during release tests to assess the transmitted shock loads.

name: Static Load Test Required
text: A static load test to demonstrate the required strength, safety factors, and margins shall be conducted.

name: Post-Static-Test Disassembly and Inspection
text: Following the static load test, the assemblies shall be completely disassembled and reinspected for possible damage.

name: Vehicle Level Acceptance Tests Shall Follow MIL-STD-1540
text: The vehicle level acceptance tests shall be conducted in accordance with the requirements of MIL-STD-1540 (SSC-S-016).

name: Video Recording of Deployment Required
text: After assembly of the deployable on the vehicle, a time correlated video recording or motion picture film of deployment shall be utilized to ensure that the dynamics of deployment are within specified criteria.

name: Record Deployment Prior to Vehicle Mounting When Needed
text: Where deployment is impractical after assembly on the vehicle, this recording shall be made during the last functional deployment prior to mounting of the deployable on the vehicle.

name: First Motion Cold Test Required
text: A first motion cold test of all deployables shall be included, where practicable, as part of the vehicle thermal testing to verify release at the acceptance level cold temperature.

name: Prelaunch Validation Tests Shall Follow MIL-STD-1540
text: The prelaunch validation tests shall be conducted in accordance with the requirements of MIL-STD-1540 (SSC-S-016).

name: Full Deployment After Vehicle Attachment
text: Where practicable, a complete deployment of deployable flight hardware in the flight configuration shall be conducted after attachment of the deployable to the vehicle.

name: Alignment Check and Initial Motion Test When Full Deployment Is Impractical
text: Where a complete deployment is not practical, an alignment check and an initial motion release test shall be conducted in lieu of the above requirements.

name: Minimum Breakaway Force Measurement
text: A measurement of the minimum breakaway force shall be made to ensure that no binding of the release mechanism or excessive friction is present.

name: Repeat 4.3.5 Inspections at Launch Site
text: Where practicable, the inspections listed in Paragraph 4.3.5 shall be repeated at the launch site after assembly of the vehicle in the flight configuration.

name: Include Contingency Cases in Prelaunch Validation
text: Prelaunch validation exercises shall include contingency cases involving anomalous operation of moving mechanical assemblies. For example, partial deployment of devices may cause additional effects on the vehicle such as changes to thermal control, inertial properties, communication degradation, or sensor blockage.

name: Inspect and Retest Bearings After Initial Flight
text: Bearings that are to be used for a number of flights shall be inspected and retested after the initial flight.

name: Conduct Individual Bearing Torque Tests
text: Individual bearing tests shall be conducted to determine if the resistive torques are within acceptable limits.

name: Refurbish Bearings When Torque Margins Are Too Low
text: If the mechanism torque or force margins are less than the minimum acceptance requirements, the bearings shall be completely inspected, refurbished, and retested as necessary after each flight.

name: Modification and Rework Shall Meet Original QA Criteria
text: Completed moving mechanical assemblies shall be modified and reworked with the same high quality assurance provisions and criteria as the original assembly.

name: Inspection and Retesting Shall Follow MIL-STD-1540
text: Inspection and retesting shall be in accordance with MIL-STD-1540 (SSC-S-016) and the requirements stated herein, or as directed by the contracting officer.

name: No Second Run-In Test Unless Rework Invalidates Original
text: Moving mechanical assemblies that have successfully completed the run-in test and are subsequently repaired, reworked, modified, or reacceptance tested shall not be given another run-in test unless the rework is so extensive as to invalidate the initial run-in.

name: Retest Assemblies Stored More Than One Year
text: Moving mechanical assemblies that are not assembled on a vehicle but are placed in storage for more than one year shall be retested in accordance with the established thermal or thermal vacuum acceptance test procedures prior to use.

name: Annual Lubricant Degradation Testing After Two Years Storage
text: After two years of storage and every year thereafter, the liquid lubricants used in these moving mechanical assemblies shall, where practicable, be sample tested to evaluate degradation.

name: Eliminate Cause of Lubricant Degradation and Relubricate
text: If there is evidence of lubricant degradation, the cause of the degradation shall be eliminated and the assembly relubricated.

name: Dimensional Analysis
text: A dimensional analysis of all moving parts and intentional interference-fit parts shall be performed and documented to ensure that specified functional performance is maintained under worst-case environmental conditions and configurations.

name: Dimensional Analysis Considerations
text: The dimensional analysis shall account for the following: a. Manufacturing, assembly, and alignment tolerances. b. Temperature- and temperature-gradient-induced deformations. c. Deflections due to vibration. d. Deflections due to external loads. e. Deflections due to operational loads. f. The full range of adjustability of the mechanism parts.

name: Establish Clearance
text: Static and dynamic clearance requirements between mechanism components and any other structure, component, thermal covering, and field of view shall be established.

name: Maintain Clearance
text: Required static and dynamic clearances between mechanism components and any other structure, component, thermal covering, and field of view shall be maintained throughout the service life and life test of the mechanism.

name: Establish Internal Clearance
text: Internal mechanism clearance requirements shall be established.

name: Maintain Internal Clearance
text: Required internal mechanism clearances shall be maintained throughout the service life and life test of the mechanism.

name: Clearance Considerations
text: The established clearance requirements shall account for the following: a. Manufacturing, assembly, and alignment tolerances. b. Temperature- and temperature-gradient-induced deformations or instabilities. c. Deflections due to vibration. d. Deflections due to external loads, including gravity effects. e. Deflections due to operational loads. f. Deflections due to changes in pressurization, including thermal blanket billowing. g. Motion of cable harnesses, tubing, and sensor wiring. h. Environments arising from transportation. i. The full range of adjustability of the mechanism parts.

name: Clearance Measurement
text: Clearance measurements shall be performed on the highest level of assembly possible.

name: Torque Margin Worst-Case Conditions
text: All torque margin requirements shall be applied under worst-case conditions throughout the mechanismâ€™s life, including throughout life testing.

name: Torque Margin at Input and Output
text: Mechanisms that use torque multipliers or reducers (e.g., gearboxes, strain wave gear drives, lever arms) shall meet torque margin requirements at both the input and output of multiplying or reducing devices.

name: Verify Torque Margin
text: All torque margins shall be verified during an acceptance test at the highest possible level of assembly.

name: Static Torque Margin
text: Static torque margin per Equation 4-1 and Table 1 shall be greater than zero within the mechanismâ€™s full range of motion.

name: Dynamic Torque Margin
text: Dynamic torque margin per Equation 4-1 and Table 1 shall be greater than zero within the mechanismâ€™s full range of motion.

name: Holding Torque Margin
text: Holding torque margin per Equation 4-1 and Table 1 shall be greater than zero at the specified positions within the mechanismâ€™s full range of motion.

name: Stepper Motor Torque Margin
text: Stepper motor torque margin shall be greater than zero within the mechanismâ€™s full range of motion, using the appropriate allowable margin calculation method per Table 2, Stepper Motor Margin Calculation Methods.

name: Stepper Motor Holding Torque Margin
text: When stepper motor detent torque is used to maintain rotor position in the presence of vibratory disturbances, detent stiffness and motor damping shall be considered when determining the holding force margin.

name: Control System Performance Margins
text: For servomechanism applications, control system performance margins shall be calculated in addition to meeting the applicable static torque margin, dynamic torque margin, holding torque margin, and stroke margin requirements.

name: Stroke Margin
text: Stroke margin requirements shall be established for all mechanisms.

name: Worst Case Stroke Margin
text: All stroke margins shall account for worst-case credible combinations of the following: a. Environmentally induced distortions. b. Misalignments. c. Dimensional tolerances. d. Load-induced distortions.

name: Bearing Not To Carry Current
text: Bearings shall not be used to carry electrical current.

name: Gear Not To Carry Current
text: Gears shall not be used to carry electrical current.

name: Electrical Bonding and Grounding
text: Mechanisms shall include electrical bonding and ground paths between moving and stationary parts sufficient to meet electromagnetic environmental effects requirements.

name: Moving Surfaces Lubricated
text: All surfaces in contact for which friction under relative motion negatively affects performance of the mechanism shall be lubricated.

name: Lubricant Selection
text: The selection of lubricants for mechanisms shall include the following considerations: a. The effect of the service environments (ground storage conditions, pressure, temperature, radiation, dust, humidity, salt spray, etc.) on lubricants. b. Creep properties of wet lubricants. c. Viscosity index (variation of viscosity with temperature) of wet lubricants. d. Elastohydrodynamic (EHD) film thickness if operating in the EHD lubrication regime. e. Protection against galling and friction welding in the boundary lubrication regime. f. Outgassing and breakdown products from wet lubricants that could contaminate sensitive surfaces. g. Polymerization of wet lubricants, particularly due to high contact pressures. h. Lubricant purity and filtration level. i. Lubricant depletion for wet lubricants. (This is typically handled through a /'lubrication loss analysis/' which considers evaporation, creep/migration, consumption, and fling.) j. Lubricant wear-out for dry lubricants. k. Generation and management of dry lubricant wear debris. l. Compatibility of each lubricant with other lubricants and other materials (substrates, platings, coatings, and preservative or shipping oils). m. Exposure to propellant or propellant vapor. n. Interaction with pyrotechnic materials and their reaction products (blowby). o. Temperature limits of the lubricants. p. Corrosion protection of the mechanism. q. Contact stress. r. Coefficient of friction needed. s. The effect of wear debris on wet lubricant properties.

name: Lubricant Evaporative Loss Analysis
text: An evaporative loss analysis shall be performed to show that 90 percent of the initial liquid lubricant quantity remains at end of life, not including lubricant degradation.

name: Indicate Critical States
text: A direct indication of the critical states of each mechanism shall be provided.

name: Structural Requirements After Failure
text: Mechanisms classified as failure tolerant shall meet all structural requirements using full design factors of safety after failure of the mechanism to operate.

name: Structural Mounting Boundary Conditions
text: Engineering analyses shall account for the structural mounting boundary conditions, including: a. Stiffness. b. Mounting alignment tolerances. c. Temperature-induced distortions. d. Load-induced distortions. e. Interface friction.

name: Survive Stall Conditions
text: The mechanism shall remain functional after exposure to stall conditions at any point in its travel.
rationale: The mechanism should not be able to break itself.

name: Non-Jamming Mechanical Stops
text: Non-jamming mechanical stops shall be incorporated into all mechanisms where exceeding required range of motion will result in detrimental effects to the mechanism or larger system.

name: Survive Stop Impact
text: Mechanism components shall maintain a positive margin of safety with the full design factors of safety applied when subjected to worst-case transient loads from mechanical stop impact.

name: Survive External Impact Loads
text: If manipulator systems, payload operations, extravehicular or intravehicular activities, or other situations presenting a risk of inadvertent contact are present, exposed mechanism components, protective shrouds and covers, and mounting structure shall be designed to accommodate inadvertent impact loads from these sources.

name: Ball Bearing ABEC Tolerances
text: Ball bearings used in high precision or low torque ripple applications shall utilize raceways that meet Annular Bearing Engineering Committee (ABEC) 7, 7P, or 7T tolerances (or better) in accordance with American Bearing Manufacturing Association (ABMA) standards (documents depend on application and are accessible at https://www.americanbearings.org/).

name: Ball Bearing Tolerances
text: Nonstandard ball bearings or thin section ball bearings where ABMA tolerances do not apply that are used in high precision or low torque ripple applications shall have the manufacturerâ€™s precision level most nearly equivalent to ABEC 7.

name: Ball Bearing Ball Material
text: Ball bearings used in high precision or low torque ripple applications shall utilize steel balls of ANSI/ABMA/ISO 3290-1, Rolling Bearings - Balls - Part 1: Steel balls, grades 3 through 10, inclusive, or ASTM F2215, Standard Specification for Balls, Bearings, Ferrous and Nonferrous for Use in Bearings, Valves, and Bearing Applications, grades 3 through 10, inclusive, or ceramic balls of ASTM F2094/F2094M, Standard Specification for Silicon Nitride Bearing Balls, grades 3C through 10C, inclusive.
Ball bearings used in high precision or low torque ripple applications shall utilize a raceway surface finish of 2.0 microinches arithmetic average (AA) or better.

Ball bearings used in high precision, low torque ripple, or long-life applications shall utilize material that has been refined using one of the following processing sequences: a. Air melting followed by Vacuum Arc Remelting (VAR, also known as Consumable Electrode Vacuum Melting or CEVM). b. Vacuum Induction Melting (VIM) followed by VAR. c. VIM followed by Pressurized Electroslag Remelting (PESR).

The mean Hertzian contact stress on the most highly loaded element in a rolling element bearing shall remain less than or equal to the appropriate values in Table 3, Allowable Contact Stress for Bearing Materials Under Non-Operational Yield Design Loads, when subjected to the non-operational yield design load.
For materials other than those listed in Table 3, an allowable contact stress shall be determined.
Bearing fatigue life calculations shall be based on the L0.05 life when subjected to maximum time-varying loads consistent with the conditions under which the L0.05 life was determined.
The upper and lower extremes of the ball bearing contact ellipses shall be contained by the raceways.

All ball bearings shall be preloaded with the following exceptions: a. Four-point (gothic arch) bearings. b. Deep groove ball bearings for which it can be shown that the absence of preload on the deep groove ball bearing is not detrimental to the performance of the mechanism. c. Wave generator bearings in strain wave gearing.

If axial sliding of a bearing ring is required to maintain preload and/or prevent axial overload, the sliding interface shall be designed to operate as a linear sliding bearing over the range of qualification environmental limits, including lubrication to reduce wear and sliding friction forces to acceptable levels throughout the service life.
Bearing preload shall be measured once all the assembly steps that establish or affect bearing preload have been completed.

Mechanisms utilizing guides or linear bearings to constrain a carriage to move in its length direction shall use a length-to-width ratio of 2:1 or greater, unless it can be shown by analysis that a length-to-width ratio of less than 2:1 will not cause the mechanism to bind or undergo stick-slip motion taking into account the following: a. Possible friction coefficients. b. Contact forces. c. Actuating forces. d. Dynamically induced forces. e. Misalignments. f. Eccentric loading.

Each electronically commutated (EC) brushless motor shall have the following characteristics measured (or calculated from measured values): a. Torque constant (Kt). b. Motor constant (Km). c. Torque versus speed curve using flight-representative drive electronics. d. Phase resistances. e. Phase inductances. f. End-to-end commutated torque performance.
The minimum measured torque output from each EC brushless motor shall be verified using flight-representative drive electronics.

Each stepper motor shall have the following performance characteristics measured: a. Powered breakaway torque. b. Unpowered (detent) torque versus angle for a full rotation. c. Pull-in torque with representative inertia, friction loads, and step rates. d. Pull-out torque with representative inertia, friction loads, and step rates. e. Step accuracy. f.
